title: Questions people actually ask
intro: Half of every conversation is questions. Get the word order right, ask politely, and check things with tags like a native.
introBn: কথোপকথনের অর্ধেকই প্রশ্ন — সঠিক ক্রম আর ভদ্র রূপ শিখে নিন।

units.title: Direct questions
units.idea: Question = (question word) + helper verb + subject + main verb. If there is no helper verb, use do, does or did.
units.ideaBn: প্রশ্নে helper verb (is, are, do, does, did, have, can) subject-এর আগে বসে।

formula.name: With be
formula.pos: Where is the meeting? Are you ready?

formula.name: With do
formula.pos: Where do you work? What did she say?

formula.name: Subject questions
formula.pos: Who called you? What happened? (no do)

uses.bn: does/did এর পরে verb-এর মূল রূপ।
uses.ex: What did you buy? (not: did you bought)

uses.rule: When who/what is the subject, no do.
uses.bn: প্রশ্নবোধক শব্দ নিজেই subject হলে do লাগে না।

uses.rule: Prepositions often go at the end.
uses.ex: Who are you talking to? Where are you from?

traps.why: Who is the subject: no did.

drills.x: Who is the subject: no did.
Helper + subject + -ing, preposition at the end.

drills.s: ___ option do you prefer, A or B?
How ___ do you visit your village?

units.title: Indirect questions (polite)
units.idea: To sound polite, start with 'Could you tell me…' or 'Do you know…' and then use normal statement word order. No do/does/did.
units.ideaBn: ভদ্রভাবে প্রশ্ন করতে Could you tell me… এর পরে সাধারণ বাক্যের ক্রম — subject আগে, verb পরে।

formula.name: Wh-
formula.pos: Could you tell me where the lift is?

formula.name: Yes/no
formula.pos: Do you know if / whether the bank is open?

uses.ex: Do you know what time it starts?

uses.rule: Yes/no questions use if or whether.
uses.ex: Can you tell me if the parcel has arrived?

uses.rule: Openers: Could you tell me, Do you know, I was wondering, Would you mind telling me.
uses.ex: I was wondering whether you are free on Monday.

traps.wrong: Can you tell me where is the station?
traps.right: Can you tell me where the station is?

traps.wrong: Do you know what time does it open?
traps.right: Do you know what time it opens?

traps.wrong: Could you tell me is he available?
traps.right: Could you tell me if he is available?

drills.q: Pick the polite and correct question.
o: Could you tell me where is the HR office?
Could you tell me where the HR office is?
Could you tell me where does the HR office?
Could you tell me the HR office where is?
drills.a: Could you tell me where the HR office is?

drills.s: Do you know ___ Mr Karim will be back?
drills.x: Do you know when + subject + verb.

drills.s: Could you tell me ___ the payment has gone through?

drills.q: আপনি কি জানেন অফিস কয়টায় খোলে?
o: Do you know what time the office opens?
Do you know what time does the office open?
Do you know what time opens the office?
You know what time the office opens?
drills.a: Do you know what time the office opens?

o: I was wondering if could you help me.
I was wondering if you could help me.
I was wondering could you help me?
I was wondering if you can to help me.
drills.a: I was wondering if you could help me.

units.title: Tag questions and short answers
units.idea: A tag checks or invites agreement: positive sentence + negative tag, negative sentence + positive tag. Short answers repeat the helper verb.
units.ideaBn: বাক্য positive হলে tag negative, বাক্য negative হলে tag positive। 'তাই না?' = tag question।

formula.name: Tags
formula.pos: You're coming, aren't you? · She didn't call, did she?

formula.name: Short answers
formula.pos: Yes, I am. · No, she didn't. · So do I. · Neither have I.

uses.rule: Use the same helper as the sentence.
I am → aren't I? Let's → shall we?
uses.ex: I'm late, aren't I? Let's start, shall we?

uses.rule: Agree: So + helper + I (positive), Neither + helper + I (negative).
uses.bn: আমিও = So do I / Neither do I।
uses.ex: 'I love biryani.' 'So do I.' 'I can't swim.' 'Neither can I.'

traps.why: Tag uses the same subject and helper.
Short answer repeats the helper of the question.

drills.s: Let's take a short break, ___ we?
'I didn't enjoy the seminar.' '___ did I.'

o: I'm late, am I not it?

drills.x: Nobody is negative → positive tag, subject they.

drills.s: 'I've never been to Japan.' '___ have I.'
drills.x: Never is negative: Neither have I.

o: What you did at the weekend?
What did you do at the weekend?
What did you did at the weekend?
What you do at the weekend did?
mastery.a: What did you do at the weekend?

mastery.s: How long ___ you been working there?

o: Do you know if is she coming?
Do you know if she is coming?
Do you know is she coming?
Do you know if she coming is?
mastery.a: Do you know if she is coming?
